note: Captured once from the published effect-dynamodb@1.40.0 and @effect-dynamodb/schema@1.40.0, installed outside the repo and run by a scratch script against DynamoDB Local. Three entities over { id, note?: string, counts: Record<string, number> } with counts configured { storedAs: SparseMap(), field: 'sr' } (prefix counts): Plain, Retained (versioned: { retain: true }) and Unique (with email, unique on it). Each case starts from a row put or upsert created with { id: 'a', counts: { a: 1 } } (email 'a@x' on Unique): put stores the map whole as sr, upsert stores entries counts#a on Plain and sr on the others. For each operation, standalone or in a transaction, its outcome (a result, or a failure's tag and the first line of its message), every request it sent (command and expression parts, a transaction's per item), every row of the table after it, and what get read back; UUIDs and timestamps are replaced by <token> and <time>. The capture under DynamoSchema.make({ escapeKeys: true }) was identical, case for case, so one record serves both. Never regenerate it: it is the record of what 1.40.0 did.
